chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), regarding two men insulting each other,
He said: The initiator of the two is more unjust, and his burden and the burden of his companion are upon him for as long as he does not apologize to the oppressed one.
ai.seo_question: Who bears more responsibility in a mutual argument according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him), the initiator of the mutual insult is deemed more unjust, bearing the sin of both parties until he actively seeks forgiveness from the aggrieved. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the initiator's greater responsibility in restoring social harmony, requiring not just cessation of hostilities but proactive reconciliation (sulh) to absolve the shared burden of sin. The hadith underscores that the moral debt remains with the aggressor until the cycle of retaliation is broken by the one who started it.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> regarding two men insulting each other.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The initiator of the two in more unjust and his burden and the burden of his companion would be upon him for as long as he does not apologise to the oppressed one’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj from abu al- Hassan Musa (a.s.) who has said the following about two people reviling: “Abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) has said, ‘
Of the two people reviling each other, the initiator is more unjust. He bears his own sin and the sin of his companion as long as he does not apologize to the oppressed.’”
